title: 2026-10-28_Coinminer_Incident_Response_Scenario_c55
description: Investigate and respond to a cryptocurrency mining malware incident on Linux servers.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The IT department has detected unusual CPU usage on several Linux servers in the network. Initial investigation suggests the presence of cryptocurrency mining malware. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the following systems with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`:
- `miner-host` (192.168.50.5)
- `second-host` (192.168.50.6)
- `pool-server` (192.168.40.5)
levels.local_content: To start the local sandbox, use the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. To proceed to the training levels, ENTER or TYPE the passkey 'start'. Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. To proceed to the training levels, ENTER or TYPE the passkey 'start'.

levels.title: Investigate the unusual CPU usage on miner-host
levels.content: The system administrator has noticed consistently high CPU usage on `miner-host`. Investigate this host to identify any suspicious processes or services that might be causing this abnormal behavior.
levels.solution:
1. Check running processes using the command: `top -c`
2. Identify suspicious services using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service`
3. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running processes and services for anything unusual or unauthorized.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `top -c` to check running processes.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to identify suspicious services.

levels.title: Analyze network connections on miner-host
levels.content: After identifying suspicious processes, examine the network connections on `miner-host` to determine if the system is communicating with any external hosts that might be related to cryptocurrency mining.
levels.solution:
1. Check network connections using the command: `netstat -tulnp`
2. Look for unusual outbound connections, especially to ports commonly used for mining pools.
3. The hidden flag is the port number used for suspicious outbound communication.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for unusual outbound connections, especially to ports commonly used for mining pools.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `netstat -tulnp` to check network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Focus on outbound connections to identify suspicious ports.

levels.title: Investigate lateral movement to second-host
levels.content: Examine `second-host` to determine if the cryptocurrency mining malware has spread from `miner-host`. Identify any evidence of lateral movement or unauthorized access.
levels.solution:
1. Check for unusual files using the command: `find / -type f -name "*.sh" 2>/dev/null`
2. Look for any scripts or tools that might indicate lateral movement.
3. The hidden flag is the name of the script or tool used to propagate the malware to `second-host`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check for any unusual files, services, or network connections that might indicate lateral movement.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `find / -type f -name "*.sh" 2>/dev/null` to search for unusual scripts.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Focus on scripts in unusual locations that might indicate lateral movement.
